## Session 15 · Round 5 PICK (measurement-tool round r355 — the skeleton scorer's autojunk cliff) — written before any code, 2026-09-17 12:50 NZST
- **Why now (§3 step 6 / the r315 precedent):** r352 named the artefact once — CHFUN06 0.0 fell 56.1 → 25.5 % when five restored `<p>` (the gold has them) pushed its skeleton from 198 to 203 lines. The cause is proven: `difflib.SequenceMatcher`'s AUTOJUNK heuristic (on by default) marks any line occurring in more than 1 % of a sequence of 200+ items as junk and never matches on it — and a skeleton is MADE of such lines ("p", "WIDGET", "div.row"). A trial scorer with `autojunk=False` on the r354 corpus (`_r355_skeleton_noautojunk.py` → `_r355_sk_noautojunk.{json,log}`): **128 pages change, 126 UP** (BLL170 0.0 14.1 → 58.2, TEFUN02 13.4 → 57.1, BLL210 14.3 → 54.8, BLL140 16.2 → 56.2, TEFUN04 14.3 → 53.3, CEDO502 1.1 18.5 → 53.3 — every long single-page Fundamentals / BLL module the dashboard has listed as a "worst page" for months), 2 down by < 1pp; **the corpus mean 50.9646 → 51.9788 % (+1.01pp), ≥ 50 % 1073 → 1093, ≥ 75 / ≥ 90 unchanged.** A measurement defect this size cannot wait for a third naming: the queue is otherwise exhausted at the floor (every remaining text-loss shape < 20 sites; the D10-3 kickoffs exhausted; no KB row; no structural class since r341), so the tooling round is the next PICK.
- **Class:** gate-configuration / measurement tool — `_skeleton_compare.py` scores with `autojunk=False` (`SKAUTOJUNK=1` restores the old numbers for a one-off comparison); every baseline that carries a skeleton number is RE-ESTABLISHED on the same corpus (`gate_baseline.json`, CLAUDE.md §9 / §14, the fast-loop snapshot, the loop's "% of achievable"), the +1.01pp recorded as an INSTRUMENT correction, never a gain. No engine or data change; no regeneration; every other gate untouched. Gate-neutral by design (neither counts toward the plateau window nor resets it).
- **Proof:** the scorer's `--selftest` GREEN; the full corpus scored with the new instrument = the trial numbers exactly; the ceiling instrument (`_measure_ceiling.py`) does not use SequenceMatcher (unchanged, 91.9 %); `% of achievable` = 51.98 / 91.9 = 56.6 % (was 55.5 %).

## Session 23 — Round 1 PICK (engine r370): the combined Writers Template's MEDIA-LIST PREAMBLE leaks into the last lesson page — written before any code, 2026-09-18 09:20 NZST
- **How it was found (not the miner's queue — a second lens).** The session-22 exhaustion verdict was TESTED, not rubber-stamped, with three instruments the miner does not have (`outputs/_s23_gap_rank.py` — pages ranked by ceiling-minus-score; `_s23_textcluster.py` — every differing line keyed by its TEXT; `_s23_button_census.py` / `_s23_journal_census.py` / `_s23_lessonsummary.py` / `_s23_addbutton.py` / `_s23_pairing_census.py`). The text-cluster lens surfaced a 12-module `EXTRA body li>a «if a specific third-party item/image is crucial …»` row (below the miner's floor because the gate pairs only 12 of the pages); the corpus-wide grep behind it: **136 Claude lesson pages / 134 modules** (Standard 85 / Fundamentals 27 / Inquiry 24) ship the Writers Template's media-list instruction bullet — "If a specific third-party item/image is crucial to your writing, then please submit this for early copyright clearance now/before starting writing [Early copyright review.docx]" — as learner-facing body text; **the gold ships it on 0 pages**; 435 WTs carry it.
- **Mechanism (triangulated BLL142 / BLL144 / ANZH203 — WT → gold → Claude).** In a COMBINED `Writers Template + Media List.docx` the media-list section opens after the last content page with a red `MEDIA LIST` heading, the red instruction "Please supply details for ALL external media …", the plain-text copyright bullet (with its sharepoint link), then the media TABLE. `ModuleResolver.PrepareRun` excludes only the TABLE block (`run.wtBlocks = TrimFrontMatter(…).filter(b => b !== mediaTable.block)`); the preamble blocks stay in the content stream: the two red runs become `Writers Note:` cv2-notes (gate-excluded chrome), the black bullet renders as `<ul><li>…<a>` on the last page. The AR-5 trailing-boilerplate rule (`PageSplitter`, after the final `[end page]`) cannot catch it: on the 134 WTs the tag before the preamble is `[body]` / `[button]` / `[image]` / a bare `[End]` (a CONTAINER_CLOSE alias, not a page boundary) — 16 have no tag within 8 lines at all.
- **Class.** Structure-only (a drop): derivable 1.00; gold consensus 1.00 in every template group (0 of 2385 gold pages carry it); pages 136 ≥ the 20-page body floor; modules 134. Authority: KB level 1 — `Input_Doc_Rules.json` `_meta.purpose` ("which parts of the Writers Template + Media List are real content, which are boilerplate to discard … a new boilerplate block = a data edit HERE") and the KB's media-list guidance (01C: the media table is data for acknowledgements, never page content). Not a gold-matching class: a template-boilerplate LEAK class (the r341 literal-leak family). Gate-visible on the 12 paired pages (EXTRA `ul` / `li` / `a` lines removed); the other 124 pages are unpaired or the bullet sits in a WIDGET-collapsed subtree — the value is learner-facing, the gate holds.
- **Fix (DATA OVER CODE).** `Input_Doc_Rules.json` gains `media_list_preamble` (enabled, env `MLPREAMBLE_OFF`, a phrase list: `media list`, `please supply details for all external media`, `third-party item/image is crucial`, `early copyright`, `add additional rows if necessary`); `DocxExtractor.TrimMediaListPreamble(blocks, tableBlock, run)` — for a COMBINED doc only (the table block is inside the WT's own blocks), walk BACKWARDS from the media table while each block is blank or matches a preamble phrase (folded, red markers stripped) and drop that run together with the table; one info note. A separate Media List docx is untouched by construction. `ModuleResolver.PrepareRun` calls it in place of the bare `.filter`.
- **Probe plan.** In-memory A/B over all 416 modules (`_ab.py MLPREAMBLE_OFF=1`), the ON pages scored with `_skeleton_compare.match()` BEFORE any regeneration (the r367 / r369 lesson); expected: 136 pages change, every change a removed `ul/li/a` (+ the two notes), no page loses content the gold has. Then a SCOPED regeneration of the 134 modules (the class is the media-list tail — its family IS the affected set), `run_all_gates.sh`, finalise.

## Session 30 — Round 4 PICK (engine r421) + what shipped — THE REGISTRY-KNOWN MODULE CODE (21 Sept ≈19:20 → 19:55 NZST)

## Session 30 — Round 4 PICK (engine r421) — THE REGISTRY-KNOWN MODULE CODE: a filename's leading token that the structure index knows is the module code (the WHA / ANZHFUN recognition gap)
- **The defect (found through F23 `nav:phases` MISSING and the r420 CHWHA note).** `ModuleResolver.DetectModuleCode` reads the code with ONE regex, `\b([A-Z]{2,6}\d{2,4}(?:RR)?)\b`, over the filenames and then the first 40 front-matter paragraphs. Four intake modules fall outside it: **CHWHA / GEWHA** (no digits), **ANZHFUN05** (seven letters), **PWYWHA1** (one digit — and its front matter mentions `PWY1000`, so it converts AS PWY1000). Their builds ship as `MODULE_0_0.html` / `PWY1000_0_0.html`, the run has no `moduleCode`, so the r408 registry rows mined for exactly these codes (`Module_Structure_Index.module_meta` has all four) are never reached — global defaults instead (ANZHFUN05 11.0 %, PWYWHA1 15.2 %, CHWHA's CJK bare under r419); the acks / manifest / interactives file names are wrong too. F23 decomposed: FRFUN06–08 = the multi-file Novice / Emergent renderer (28 pages / 3 modules — the s28 follow-up, a build); JPFUN01 / 02 = the `[Novice Content starts here]` marker dialect the r265 level-page machinery does not read (2 modules); MXFUN01–03 = the dual-build gold pairing (needs-Chris); ANZHFUN05 = this defect; ARFUN04 / SSFUN07 singletons.
- **The fix (a recognition defect, not a gold-matching class — the PMT101-style item; DATA OVER CODE):** `Input_Doc_Rules.module_code_detection.registry_token {enabled, env CODEREG_OFF, separators}` — between the filename regex and the front-matter regex, each filename's LEADING token (split on space / underscore / dot / dash, upper-cased) that is a key of `ModuleStructureIndex.module_meta` is a candidate ("filename — a registry-known code"), so a code the regex cannot shape still resolves when the corpus registry knows it; the regex keeps precedence (an unchanged path for every module it already names), the front-matter regex stays the last resort. Expected: exactly CHWHA, GEWHA, ANZHFUN05, PWYWHA1 change (their outputs renamed to the code; their registry rows reached).
- **Gate expectations:** the four modules' pages re-pair under their real names (CHWHA `MODULE_0_0` → `CHWHA_0_0`; PWYWHA1 `PWY1000_0_0` → `PWYWHA1_0_0`) — skeleton movement on ≤ 6 pages; every other module byte-identical (the probe proves it).
- **What shipped (r421, build 260619.92, 21 Sept ≈19:55):** `Input_Doc_Rules.module_code_detection.registry_token {enabled, env CODEREG_OFF, separators, min_length}` + `ModuleResolver.DetectModuleCode` step 1b — when the filename regex names nothing, each filename's leading token that is a key of `ModuleStructureIndex.module_meta` is a candidate ahead of the front-matter regex. Probe OFF (`CODEREG_OFF`) = disk 2555 / 2555; ON exactly the 4 modules (CHWHA / GEWHA / ANZHFUN05 / PWYWHA1), each output renamed to its code, nothing else changed. Scored against the gold before regenerating: CHWHA 41.0 → 43.9 (its registry row + the r419 CJK wrap now firing), GEWHA 25.9 → 25.8, ANZHFUN05 11.0 → 9.1 (its row gives `body.fundamentals`, no menu and the fundamentals footer — the gold's own — but the Novice / Emergent two-tile page is unbuilt, difflib re-aligns lower), PWYWHA1 15.2 → 13.8 — net −0.6pp-sum, NAMED and accepted (`_fastloop_diff.py --commit --accept-named`, `_s30_r421_fastloop_named.log`). SCOPED regeneration of the 4 + 12 spot-checks (0 stale; 12 / 12; containment 4 ⊆ 4; the ledger scoped #5 since the r416 FULL — 3 of headroom). `run_all_gates.sh`: skeleton 54.2067 → 54.2065 % (−0.0002pp; 0 movers on the unchanged pages, 4 renamed), ≥50 1441 / ≥75 238 / ≥90 20 / RAW 38.229 EXACT; cs 14170 / 186 / 683 / 23, body 54 / 5 / 190 / 247, clean 2504 / 2548, leak 73 / 44, tags 9557 — all EXACT; every verifier ✓; 17 selftests GREEN; feature index GREEN; miner 182 → 182; checksums refreshed. Follow-ups recorded from F23: the FRFUN multi-file Novice / Emergent renderer (28 pages / 3 modules — a build), the JPFUN `[Novice Content starts here]` marker alias for the r265 level pages (2 modules), the MXFUN dual-build pairing (needs-Chris).

  `/mnt/c/Users/Gavin/TeKura/FINAL_MODULE_DATA`). WSL has Node v22.23.2, Python 3.14.4, git 2.53.0.
- **Why:** native Windows Node/Python cannot open files through the project's symlinks
  (`CONVERTER_V2/app` -> EACCES, `CONVERTER_V2/data` -> EINVAL), so every gate fails natively; WSL
  traverses them and `_MIGRATION/verify_after_transfer.sh` = PASS under WSL. Windows Python also
  defaults to a non-UTF-8 locale encoding, which the tools do not guard against.
- **Git commits are made with Windows git (2.55) from Git Bash** in `pageforge-site`. Never push.
- WSL `/tmp` persists between calls. Timings under WSL: defect audit ~10 s, ceiling tool ~60 s, KB facts ~55 s,
  16-shard census + dashboard ~4 min.
- Tool quirks: long file writes go through the Write tool (a ~30 KB heredoc hits ENAMETOOLONG); ONE heredoc
  per shell call (two heredocs in one call break the tool's quoting); commit messages from a file (`git commit -F`).
  Gold page filenames use the dot form `XMES101.02.html` (a `*2.0.html` glob finds nothing); gold dirs are
  nested under the template folder (`01-Finalized_Modules_/Standard/XMES101`) — resolve with `_corpus.mdir`.
  `grep` reports `InteractiveBuilder.js` as binary — use `grep -a`.
- `CONVERTER_V2/outputs/` and `reference/` are OUTSIDE the git repo; loop artefacts are mirrored into
  `pageforge-site/converter-v2/loop/` at each commit (see its README).
- `_regen_safe.sh` hard-codes `timeout 40` (the old sandbox wall): run `batch_convert.cjs` directly with a long
  timeout for regenerations, then prove freshness with `_content_manifest.py fresh --affected`.

**THE ROUND: `inquiry_tabs.template_fallback` (data flag `enabled`, env `INQFALLBACK_OFF`).** Fires only when the module's `module_meta.template_type` is `Inquiry`, the page model is single-file, and NONE of the five existing modes fired. In fallback mode every top-level panel opener pushes the existing `INQ_SENTINEL` (an open activity is closed first, as the other modes do): a `[Tab N …]` item in any of the three label forms (a leading run of ≥ 3 consecutive labelled tabs is the writer's crumb LIST — consumed, its labels captured, never rendered — the r100 capture), a `[Page N]` / `[Lesson N]` / `[Lesson N content]` PAGE_BOUNDARY opener, or an `[End page]` closer followed by more content (de-duplicated against an opener that follows it). Labels, in order: the writer's list entry for that panel index; the opener's own label (the black text after a bare `[Tab N]` / `[LESSON N]`, or the text inside the red span after the tag words — the r422 `navLabelOf` rule); else the panel's first heading with a leading `Lesson N:` stripped (the r111 form); the first panel is the intro (`Introduction`, `Intro` for the CED prefix — a per-prefix `intro_label` map). ## Session 35 — Round 2 (engine r431, build 260620.04, 22 Sept ≈17:56 → ≈18:40) — THE OVERVIEW MENU'S INNER-WORD LABEL OVER-FIRE + what shipped

**PICK (22 Sept ≈17:56 → 18:02; the miner's module-menu lane — the chrome region's EXTRA rows #48 `div.col-12.col-md-8 › Claude h5` (81 pages / 25 modules) and #49 (`p`); authority §1b level 3, the gold's own menu region; measured by `_s35_r2_menuover.py` → `.log`).** Round 1's census left CEDO204's page-1 content (`Why do birds build nests?` … `How do spiders build webs?`) inside `div#module-menu-content`; the corpus census of menu-region text the paired GOLD keeps in its BODY: **56 pages / 34 modules / 213 elements**, concentrated (MXFUN03 32, CHFUN05 31, CEDR302 24, CEDO204 22, ENGJ201 14 over 6 pages, the rest 1–8). The mechanism behind CEDO204 / TWHK901 (`Reflect: What can you do …`) / part of CEDR302 (`What do I know?`) is exact (`ContentConverter.#partitionItems`, the content-based overview fallback for a page with no `[MODULE INTRODUCTION]`): `matchesLabel` accepts a heading that CONTAINS a `menu.overview_section_labels` entry as an inner word — `f.includes(" " + l + " ")` / `f.endsWith(" " + l)` — so with the single-word labels "do" / "know" / "understand" every question heading ("Why do birds build nests?", "What do birds use …", "How do spiders …") opens a menu section and its block leaves the body for the menu. A single-word label is a section label only at the START of the heading or as the whole heading (the gold's `Understand` / `Know` / `Do` menu blocks); the inner-word and end-word tests stay for the multi-word labels ("how will i know", "what do i need to get started"). The probe is the measurement (the engine's own matcher over every page): expected — the over-fired blocks return to the body on CEDO204 / TWHK901 / CEDR302 and any page with a mid-heading "do" / "know" / "understand"; the gold's real menu sections unchanged (they start with the label); the PICK predicts a skeleton move ≥ 0.02pp only if the class is wider than the three named pages — otherwise a small gain, chrome-visible (the menu's EXTRA h5 / p rows shrink). MXFUN03 / CHFUN05 / ENGJ201's overrun is a different mechanism (Fundamentals / a tabs widget inside the menu; a `[Lesson Overview]` page family) — recorded, not this round.

## Session 36 — Round 5 (DECLINED on measurement, no engine change, 23 Sept 01:25 → ≈01:50) — THE MODULE MENU'S SECTION CONTENT IS A LIST + the verdict

**PICK (23 Sept 01:25; the miner's module-menu rows #36 / #37 / #49 on the r436 corpus).** Row #49 (`module-menu EXTRA div.col-12.col-md-6.paddingR › gold — vs Claude p>b`, 23 pages / 23 modules, consensus **1.00**, KB-tagged) read by content: on the BLL overviews Claude ships the writer's `__**Reading:**__ Students develop basic literacy capability…` lines as `<p><b>` inside the menu's left column, where the gold has `<li>` items (reworded — the text half is class C, the STRUCTURE is not). Its mirrors are rows #36 (`MISSING ul li`, 133 pages / 82 modules, derivable 0.84) and #37 (`MISSING div.col-12.col-md-8 ul`, 173 pages / 46 modules, 0.90). Measured two ways: (a) by WT line (`_s36_r5_menubold.py`) — a bold-labelled menu line is `p` in the gold 147 times and `li` 29, so the LINE-level rule is wrong corpus-wide; (b) **by MENU, structure only, no text matching (`_s36_r5_menuchild.py`, 453 paired overview menus with ≥ 3 content children on both sides): the gold's menu sections are LIST-dominant on 428 of 453 = 0.945** (p-dominant 10, tie 8), and Claude already matches on 397 — **the gap is 27–28 modules where Claude is paragraph-dominant** (CBI1004 / 1005, CEDK501, CEDO501 / 502, CEDR302 / 501, CEDT101 / 501, CEDW501, CHI1003, ENGJ102, GER1002, GEWHA, HIS1002, MUS1004, MXDB301, MXDI301, MXEX301, MXFU302, TEDC401, XDLS902–906 / 909). Their `li` counts already match the gold's (MXDI301 24 / 24, MXEX301 28 / 29) — the defect is the EXTRA paragraphs beside them (MXDI301 38 vs the gold's 4), i.e. the writer typed those items as plain lines and `ListsAndRuns.renderBlackText` only makes an `<li>` from a line that starts with `•` or a number. The overrun probe (`_s36_r5_overwhat2.log`) confirms the text is not over-captured: it is in the gold's menu too, as list items. **KB 01B's module-menu form is `<h5>` label + `<ul><li>` items** (the lesson-page example, the overview tab-set rule and constraint 70's "no `<p>` between a heading and its list" all assume it), so authority is §1b level 1 with the corpus at 0.945 behind it. Chrome floor: 27 modules ≥ 10. Predicted: those modules' overview menus up; the 10 gold=p menus (8 NCEA1, 2 Leaving to Learn) are the expected named dips. **Not taken in the same pass:** CEDR302's overview menu holds 89 elements (24 of them the gold puts in inquiry panels / accordions / activities) — a single-module menu-region overrun, below floor, recorded in the Follow-up section.

**THE VERDICT (23 Sept ≈01:50).** Built behind `menu.section_content_is_list` / `MENULIST_OFF` (MenuBuilder's `flushText` prefixing the corpus bullet glyph to every buffered line once a section heading had been emitted in that column, so the existing list machinery rendered them; a `max_words` guard kept genuine prose as paragraphs). The five-module probe changed four overview pages and scored them **SCAFFOLD +0.0 each** with RAW split (MXDI301 +7.6, XDLS906 −7.6). The follow-up measurement settled it: the gold's own overview-menu content is **9,732 `li` to 2,881 `p` (0.772)** and Claude already ships **0.743** — the two are less than three points apart, so the 27 "paragraph-dominant" modules are not a defect class but modules whose writers supplied more prose, which the human keeps as prose. A per-line rule would push Claude to ≈ 1.00 list and overshoot the human by a quarter of the menu's content. REVERTED: `MenuBuilder.js` is byte-identical to HEAD (`git diff` empty) and a 7-module probe (MXDI301, MXEX301, XDLS906, TEDC401, GEWHA, CEDR302, BLL125) is **34 / 34 identical to disk**; the corpus was never regenerated. The verdict is recorded in `Emit_Templates.json` as `menu._declined_r437_section_content_is_list` — the data file is the place a later round will look — and under Declined classes here. What would re-open it: a DISCRIMINATOR at the line level (what makes one menu line an item and the next a paragraph), not the menu-level dominance statistic.

## Session 37 — Round 1 (DECLINED — the activity-box boundary) + what it found

## Session 37 — Round 1 (no engine change — DECLINED on measurement) — THE ACTIVITY-BOX BOUNDARY, KEYED ON THE WRITER'S SHAPE

**PICK.** The s36 handover's unbuilt angle (1) — "a paired census of the ACTIVITY-BOX boundary keyed on the WRITER'S shape rather than on the rendered box"; s36's `_s36_r7_actbound.py` keyed on the OUTPUT, matched 4,617 boxes by title and reported over-capture 2,410 / under-capture 1,572, a population it could only call "diffuse". Authority §1b(2) the gold, with a KB-first check. No engine file was opened, so no in-flight marker was raised (§3 step 1 raises it before code is edited; this round never reached step 4).

**Three instruments, and the first two were WRONG — the finding is why.**
1. `_s37_r1_actclose.py` — reads the writer tag at the seam. Its first run was swamped by `[/red text]` (729 of 1,614 under-captures), an inline colour close that says nothing about a boundary; skipping inline markup and reading the last STRUCTURAL tag gave `[Activity N]` 395 boxes / 138 modules, which looked like a merge class.
2. `_s37_r1_actmerge.py` — characterised those 395: **395 / 395** a bare `[Activity NX]` opener with its title and lead text inline. **The class was an ARTEFACT.** ANZH101_2_0's «Tessellations» is the worked example: the gold's 2D box *does* carry "Let's use whales…" — the gold folds three sentences into one `<p>` and Claude splits them, so every element hashes differently. **Both s36's instrument and this one were comparing the SET OF ELEMENTS, which conflates a boundary defect with a paragraph-splitting difference.** That is why the population looked diffuse to s36: it was measuring the wrong thing.
3. `_s37_r1_actbound2.py` / `_actbound3.py` — the corrected instrument: compare the box's CONCATENATED text, so a boundary shows as a prefix/suffix relation and paragraphing is invisible.

**The KB-first check stopped a false class.** The corrected instrument's seam text was repeatedly the writer's own production note. Corpus-wide the writer-note phrase is **7,194 occurrences / 519 modules in Claude against 29 / 9 in the gold**, and the whole red-note family (`_s37_r1_rednote.py`) is **11,321 elements = 5.55 % of everything Claude emits on the 2,500 paired pages, against 1,604 = 0.64 % of the gold's**, on 87.8 % of paired pages (median 5.7 % of the page, max 43.5 %); by prefix Writers Note 6,899 / Designer-Developer To Do 2,594 / Red Flag 1,594 / Note from {author} 234. **KB constraints 37, 57, 59 and 88 REQUIRE every one of them** as a visible red bold `<p>` — comments have shipped to live modules and been missed — and constraint 81(c) excludes the family from Compare Mode in both directions as "developer scaffolding … never module content". The human gold has ACTIONED and REMOVED them in production. **A NAMED KB OVERRIDE (§1b): never re-open as a gold-matching class.**
**And it costs the score nothing:** 6,115 of 6,116 sampled red-note elements carry `cv2-note` / `cv2-comment`, which **round 72 already excludes from the skeleton**. The instrument was already right; only the two box censuses were reading the noise. Re-run with the family excluded from both sides, identical boxes go **236 -> 559** (+323 boxes that looked defective and are perfect).

**The measured verdict, on the corrected instrument over 4,616 paired boxes (red-note family excluded, i.e. what the gate actually sees):** identical 559 / **ends LATE 565** (228 modules) / **ends EARLY 391** (166) / starts EARLY 3 / starts LATE 1 / same-text-different-split 50 / **neither a prefix nor a suffix 3,047** (402). **NO SEAM SHAPE REACHES THE FLOOR**: in ends-LATE the top writer tag is `[body]` at 27 boxes / 24 modules and 415 of 565 seams are not in the WT dump at all; every other shape is single figures. **DECLINED — there is no derivable activity-box boundary class.**

**Where the mass actually is (`_s37_r1_disjoint.py` decomposes the 3,047):** **1,935 = 63.5 % are the un-built-widget hand-off population** — 1,062 a Claude `cv2-int-ref` box where the gold shipped no widget markup (319 modules) + 873 a Claude hand-off against a BUILT gold widget (296 modules); then 640 a genuine text difference (223), 267 both sides built differently (147), 205 the gold built a widget and Claude built nothing (124). **This is D10-3 / Needs Chris #4, and it sizes that decision far above the 844 boxes it has been carrying: 1,935 PAIRED ACTIVITY BOXES alone.** By refused type (`_s37_r1_handoff.py`, the 1,062): **dragAndDrop 414 / 213 modules**, **unclassified 326 / 153**, typing 69 / 37, reorder 51 / 40, selfCheck 33 / 21, carousel 23 / 11, memoryGame 21 / 16, then a tail all under 20.

**What this closes and what it opens.** Angle (1) of the s36 handover is DISPOSITIONED: the activity-box boundary is not a class, and the reason two sessions called it diffuse is now known and fixed in the instrument. The `unclassified` 326 boxes / 153 modules is NOT a build question — it is the scanner failing to classify a writer tag at all — and it becomes Round 2. ## Session 37 — Round 2 (engine r438, DECLINED) + what it found

## Session 37 — Round 2 (engine r438) — THE WRITER NAMES THE WIDGET IN THE FREE TEXT BESIDE THE OPENER — PICK

**THE CLASS.** The scanner emits an `unclassified` hand-off when it sees `[Activity N]` with a data table ahead and NO recognised interactive keyword inside the brackets. Its own red flag says what is missing: *"Activity has a data table but NO recognised interactive keyword — widget type must be identified from the captured content."* Very often the writer HAS named the type — in the free text beside the tag rather than inside it. ANZH104 3A: `[Activity embedded]  word find` / `[H3] 3A Clothing Word Find` / a TABLE of clothing words. `word find` is a registered alias of the `word find` tag in `Tag_Lexicon.json`.

**The mechanism already exists and throws the answer away.** `TagNormaliser` (round 217, `qualifier_alias_demote`) already folds a span's free text and scans it for any INTERACTIVE alias ≥ 4 characters — but only as a BOOLEAN (`namesWidget`) used to decide keep-or-demote. The alias it matched is discarded and never reaches the bundle. So the converter already knows how to find the writer's word; it just never uses it to classify.

**MEASURED (`_s37_r2_unclass.py`, all 1,085 unclassified hand-offs on disk).** The writer names a known widget type in the opener window on **218 = 20.1 %** (129 modules); 398 = 36.7 % name nothing; 469 = 43.2 % the opener could not be located in the WT dump (a locator limit — the 218 is a LOWER BOUND). Types named: **flip card 58 / 27 modules**, drag and drop 35 / 29, word select 35 / 30, memory game 13 / 13, sketcher 10 / 10, typing quiz 9 / 5, radio quiz 7 / 7, mcq 7 / 6, then a tail under 5.

**SCOPED TO ONE WIDGET TYPE — flipCard (D10-3: one widget type per kickoff, largest un-built population first).** `InteractiveBuilder` has a `flipCard` builder already (`case "flipCard"`), so classification reaches a real build rather than relabelling a placeholder.

**TRIANGULATION (`_s37_r2_flip.py`) — 67 boxes / 35 modules, and THE GOLD BUILT A FLIP CARD ON 56 OF 67 = 0.836**, well above the §3 step-3 floor of 0.60. Families: BLL 62, MXFL 3, TEFUN 2, ENGI 1.
**The §3 step-1 NEW-FAMILY CHECK passes:** the consensus does NOT collapse outside the dominant family — BLL 52 / 62 = **0.839**, non-BLL 4 / 5 = **0.80** (TEFUN03 2 / 2, ENGI400 1 / 1, MXFL204 1 / 1, MXFL203 0 / 2). BLL simply uses the shape most; it is not a BLL dialect, and BLL is not one of the 24 September-intake family bases. The 11 misses are named: BLL114 2E, BLL117 2D, BLL125 1E, BLL137 2A, BLL177 1E, BLL211 1A, BLL215 1A, BLL221 1C, BLL231 1C, MXFL203 10J / 10K.
Authority §1b(2) the gold, with the KB-first check clear (no KB rule assigns a widget type from free text; constraint A1 "the writer tag decides the component" is the governing principle and this round reads the writer's own naming of it). Classification: **B (instructions)**.

**PREDICTION.** Gate-visible: each classified box stops being a `cv2-int-ref` placeholder and becomes a built flipCard, so the skeleton's WIDGET marker replaces a placeholder subtree on ~56 pages. Judged per §4's widget-BUILD rule on the dashboard's flipCard *Still a box* count, with the skeleton and every protected gate required to hold-or-improve.

- **ROUND 438 IN FLIGHT — NOT PROVEN.** Class: the free-text-named widget type classifies an otherwise-unclassified activity bundle, scoped to flipCard. Files: `app/js/InteractiveScanner.js` (the unclassified-bundle branch, ~line 150), `data/Interactive_Boundary_ChildTag_Bank.json` (`_meta.opener_rule.unclassified_activity_lead.free_text_type`). Data flag: `free_text_type` (`enabled`, `types: ["flip card"]`, `min_alias`). Env toggle: **`FREETEXTTYPE_OFF`**. Affected set for the scoped ship: the 35 modules in `_s37_r2_flip.log`.

## Declined classes s37-r3 / s37-r2, full text (verbatim, s39 §5d condense #5)

- **Session 37 Round 3 (23 Sept ≈08:30) — THE FOOTER'S NAVIGATION LINK SET (the miner's chrome rows F26 / F27 / F29 / F30 and ranked rows #4–#5) — DECLINED: no discriminator; the rates already match.** The miner puts four footer rows near the top of the queue (F26 283 pages / 128 modules, F27 112 / 110 at consensus 0.88, F29 77 / 77 at 0.86, F30 70 / 69), and footer is chrome, which §3 step 1 ranks before body. **Two instrument faults had to be fixed before the numbers meant anything, and both are worth keeping.** (1) **The human COMMENTS a link out rather than deleting it** — a module's last gold page ships `<!-- <li><a href="" id="next-lesson" …></li> -->` (AGH1003_08.0). A regex over raw text counts that as PRESENT and inverts the result: the first run reported 156 last pages where "the gold keeps Next and Claude drops it", and every one was a commented-out link, i.e. the two sides AGREE. The skeleton's HTML parser drops comments, so stripping them is also what every protected gate sees. (2) **`home-nav` is a CLASS, not an id** (`<a href="" class="home-nav">`) — matching it with `id=` made it invisible in the whole first measurement, and it is precisely the fact F27 / F29 turn on. With both fixed: **2,497 paired pages, 2,254 AGREE = 90.3 %**, and `home-nav` is present on both sides everywhere (a constant, not the discriminator). By position the converter's positional rule is already the human's — overview 89 % agree, first lesson page 96 %, middle 95 %. **The residue has no rule in it.** On the LAST page (390 pages, 71 % agree) the disagreement runs BOTH ways — 61 pages the gold keeps Next and Claude drops it, 32 the reverse — because **the gold itself is split**: last-page prev-only 291 = 0.76 against prev+next 90, and **Claude already sits at 0.79**. The rates match; only the per-page assignment differs, and no discriminator separates them — the r437 menu-list precedent exactly. Of the 128 pages where Claude emits Next and the gold does not, 48 are page-count differences (29 the gold has more pages, 19 Claude does) = **Needs Chris #6**, and the 136 single-page modules are split by TEMPLATE (Fundamentals gold (none) 0.76, Inquiry gold prev+next 0.76) with Claude already agreeing on 113 of 136 = 83 %; the largest coherent miss is 8 CEDT modules, below the chrome floor of 10. **Also dispositioned in the same pass — the empty-Claude-menu pages** (`_s37_r3_nomenu.py`; the miner's module-menu census is the largest derivable chrome region at 5,451 misses / 729 pages / 204 modules): of the 175 pages with an empty Claude menu and a gold menu of ≥ 8 items, **88 / 24 modules are the s36-DECLINED KB override** (the gold repeats the module overview), **44 / 19 are gold-invented with no WT source**, and the **43 pages / 22 modules that ARE derivable break into sub-shapes each below floor** — the BLL «learningintentions» form is the r432 residue at 7 modules, ANZH404's «understand» form is 1. Scripts: `_s37_r3_footer.py`, `_s37_r3_footer2.py`, `_s37_r3_single.py`, `_s37_r3_nomenu.py`, each with its `.log`.
- **Session 37 Round 2 (23 Sept ≈07:50) — THE WIDGET TYPE THE WRITER NAMED IN THE FREE TEXT (engine r438) — DECLINED on measurement; the engine change was built, probed and REVERTED.** The unclassified path fires when no interactive keyword sits INSIDE the brackets, and its own red flag says the type "must be identified from the captured content" — which the writer often has done just outside them (`[Activity embedded]  word find`, ANZH104 3A). TagNormaliser's round-217 `qualifier_alias_demote` path ALREADY scans folded free text for INTERACTIVE aliases and discards the alias, using it only as a boolean; the round exposed that scan as `FindWidgetAlias` and classified the bundle with it, scoped to `flip card` alone (D10-3). **IT FAILED BECAUSE THE CENSUS WAS NOT MEASURING WHAT THE SCANNER CAN SEE.** `_s37_r2_unclass.py` read a 700-character window of the RAW Writers Template: 218 of 1,085 unclassified hand-offs name a known type (flip card 67 boxes / 35 modules, gold agreement **0.836**, consensus holding outside the dominant family — BLL 0.839, non-BLL 0.80). The scanner sees only the opener's own tail plus the black runs up to the first table, and on that text the population is **15 pages / 7 modules** (BLL157 / BLL160 / BLL170 / BLL177 / MXFL203 / MXFL204 / TEFUN03) — **BELOW BOTH FLOORS, a five-fold over-count.** BLL140 3F–7F is the worked example the census counted: the scanner's text reads "flip THE CARDS over", not "flip cards", so no flip alias matches. **Three findings to keep.** (a) **Free-text alias matching false-positives on ordinary prose** — on those same BLL140 openers the scan returned `memory` (an alias of `memory game`) out of running instruction text; only the `types` allow-list stopped five boxes being typed a memory game, so any future form MUST stay type-scoped and needs a POSITIONAL guard, not just a 4-character minimum. (b) The gold disagrees on 2 of the 15 (MXFL203 10J / 10K build no flip card). (c) **Classifying is not building** — `InteractiveBuilder` declines the un-paired table form, so the box stayed a placeholder merely reading `flipCard` instead of `unclassified`, while the type change shifted activity ownership downstream (TEFUN03: a paragraph moved to its own row, `alertActivity` became `alert top`) — a regression risk for a cosmetic gain. Reverted: `InteractiveScanner.js` and `TagNormaliser.js` byte-identical to HEAD; the 35 regenerated modules restored and **`_content_manifest.py fresh` reports 0 truly stale** (flipCard 524 → 510, unclassified 2308 → 2322 — exactly the 14 boxes back). The verdict is recorded in `Interactive_Boundary_ChildTag_Bank.json` `unclassified_activity_lead._declined_r438_free_text_type`. Never re-open without BOTH a census over the SCANNER'S OWN text and a builder that can read a face table. Scripts: `_s37_r2_unclass.py`, `_s37_r2_flip.py`, `_s37_r2_flip.log`.

- **Mechanism (`_s41_r1_items.cjs`, `_s41_r1_blocks.cjs`, `_s41_r1_trim.cjs`):** every TRR / PNR Writers Template types its `[TITLE BAR]` inside a bilingual TABLE cell (block 13–20, right after the Subject / Course / Module Code table). `IsContentStart` reads paragraphs only, so the module opens LATER — at `[LESSON 1 CONTENT]` (TRR102 / 103 / 109 / 111), `[LESSON 2 CONTENT]` (TRR106 / 304), a paragraph `[TITLE BAR]` (TRR110), or, with no standard start at all, the r?? fallback's first paragraph tag (TRR107 an `[Image]` in lesson 2; TRR108 `[H3] Karakia`; TRR112 / 113 the `[H1]` after `[Lesson 1]`; TRR114 `[Alert Solid]`; TRR116 a `[Side Alert]` in LESSON 5). Everything between is trimmed as front matter.
- **Size (`_s41_r1_tbgap.cjs` / `_s41_r1_where.cjs`):** 13 modules; the trimmed blocks per module 3–57 (TRR116 57 = the overview + lessons 1–4; TRR106 32; TRR107 13; TRR304 13); each trimmed overview table's text sits on the gold `_0.0` page at 0.43–0.90 (TRR102 0.87 / 0.74 / 0.43 / 0.43 / 0.68 / 0.72; TRR116 0.90 … and its lesson tables on gold 1.0–4.0 at 0.28–0.77). Gold overlap of the whole trimmed gap 0.48–0.78 in 10 modules (TRR112 0.26, TRR113 0.10, TRR107 0.30). Census over all 529 Writers Templates (`_s41_r1_openers_all.log`): a table-cell title bar before the start occurs ONLY in TRR / PNR; PNR101–107 and TRR203 / 301 already open at `[Content for DROP DOWN MENU]` (r212) BEFORE their title-bar table → unchanged by construction.
- **Authority:** the writer's own `[TITLE BAR]` tag (the content-start rule, `Input_Doc_Rules.content_start`: "real module content starts at the first RED span that opens the document") — structure the WT states; a recognition defect with the content's gold consumer measured (A — derivable). Family dialect (§1d exception 1): keyed on a template SHAPE only the TRR family has. Floor: 13 modules / ≥ 13 overview pages + TRR116's 5 missing lesson pages.
- **Rule:** when a TABLE block holds a cell whose red span resolves to `title bar` and it sits BEFORE the start the chain found (or no start was found), the document opens at that table. Data `content_start.table_title_bar_opener` {enabled}; env `TABLETB_OFF`.
